content: If you miss a dose of this medication, contact your doctor or pharmacist immediately to establish a new dosing schedule. For storage, refer to the product instructions and consult your pharmacist for specific details. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless explicitly instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in July 2024. Important Usage Information: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific condition. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete details about this product and your individual health needs. How to Use: This medication is administered via injection into a vein or muscle as directed by your doctor, typically once daily. If injected into a vein, it should be administered slowly over 1 to 2 hours. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience leakage, redness, or pain during the intravenous injection. If you are administering this medication at home, ensure you have been thoroughly trained by your healthcare professional on preparation and usage. Before use, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration. Do not use the liquid if either is present. Side Effects: Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, unusual taste or dryness in the mouth, dizziness, diarrhea, or redness, pain, or leakage at the injection site. While serious side effects are possible, your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Precautions: Before using pentamidine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Pentamidine may lead to a condition affecting heart rhythm (QT prolongation). The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. Low potassium or magnesium levels in the blood can also heighten this risk, particularly if you are using certain medications (e.g., diuretics or water pills) or experiencing conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use (including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Notes: Laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., kidney/liver function, blood pressure, blood sugar, complete blood counts, EKGs) should be conducted before starting this medication, during its use, and after completing treatment. Attend all medical and laboratory appointments as scheduled. Missed Dose: It is crucial to receive each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly to determine a new dosing schedule. Storage: Follow the product instructions and consult your pharmacist for storage details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last updated in July 2024.
